rv.q: Jan Maxwell and Rosemary Harris are giving the kinds of performances that turn agnostics into true believers.
When the servants are just as winning as the leads, that tells you this is one regal and enjoyable “Royal Family.”
Doug Hughes' sumptuous joy of an old-fashioned revival, including a keepsake performance by the legendary Rosemary Harris.
The production does find a workable comic footing, and its lead performers rise to the occasion in sparkling turns.

This revival of the Kaufman-Ferber comedy about a theatrical dynasty is blessed with a stellar cast led by Rosemary Harris, but it feels more like a museum piece than a living, breathing work of theater.
Thanks to Maxwell and Rogers, for the moment their bygone spirit is burning brightly once again.
What this love letter to the stage needed are a few more of these and some stamps of quirkiness to make this "Royal Family" a truly special delivery.
Under the assured direction of Doug Hughes, this Royal Family is indeed royal entertainment, even if it doesn't always sparkle with the brilliance that Kaufman and Ferber undoubtedly intended.
